learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn how to flip sentences around like a ninja by changing who does the action and who receives it!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🏃 Active Voice (The Doer is the Star)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: In an active sentence, the subject is the superhero doing the action. It is direct and easy to read! For example, 'The cat chased the mouse.' The cat is the subject, and it is doing the chasing.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🛋️ Passive Voice (The Receiver is the Star)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: In a passive sentence, we flip things around! The person or thing receiving the action becomes the star at the beginning of the sentence. For example, 'The mouse was chased by the cat.'

main_concepts.concept_title: 🔍 When Do We Use Passive Voice?
main_concepts.simple_explanation: We use passive voice when the action is more important than who did it, or if we do not know who did it! Like saying 'My bicycle was stolen' (we do not know who stole it).
When we change an active sentence to a passive one, we often use the word 'by' before the person who did the action. It acts like a bridge to show who caused the event!

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Sentence Flipper
fun_activity.instructions: Write down the active sentence 'My mom baked a delicious cake.' Now, be a grammar ninja and flip it into the passive voice making 'a delicious cake' the star!

quick_recap: ⭐ In Active Voice, the subject performs the action.
⭐ In Passive Voice, the subject receives the action.
⭐ Passive voice is useful when the doer is unknown or less important.
⭐ We frequently use the preposition 'by' in passive sentences to show who did it.
